chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali al-Maythami, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: “O Ya’qūb! Have you ever seen an owl during the day breathe?” I replied, “No.” He said, “Do you know why that is?” I replied, “No.” He said, “Because during the day it remains fasting upon what Allāh has sustained it with. When night covers it, it breaks its fast upon what it has been given sustenance. Then it continues chanting/lamenting over al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) until morning.”
ai.seo_question: Why do owls not breathe during the day according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Ṣādiq’s (a.s.) explanation of the owl’s nocturnal lament as a cosmic sign of mourning for Ḥusayn (a.s.), illustrating how creation participates in the Ahl al-Bayt’s grief. This tradition underscores the Shia concept of *alam al-nabawi* (the prophetic world), where natural phenomena reflect spiritual realities, specifically the enduring sorrow for the Imam of the Age. The owl’s continuous chanting until dawn symbolizes the perpetual nature of this lamentation, linking the physical world to the metaphysical realm of the Imams.
